title: Package Helm charts for offline bundles + emit chart digests into bundle manifest
author: Devon Price
description:
Context: Redwood Private offline installs require a single offline bundle containing everything needed for install/upgrade, with offline verification. As part of the v1 bundle format, we need to include Helm charts as packaged artifacts and record a digest for each chart in the bundle manifest so the installer can validate integrity offline.

This PR adds a deterministic chart packaging step (produces .tgz) and exports chart digests (sha256) for inclusion in the offline bundle manifest. It also normalizes a few chart metadata fields that were causing `helm package` output differences across environments.

What changed (high level): 1) New packaging script/target that packages charts in a deterministic way (stable file ordering + fixed mtimes + gzip without timestamp) so the same chart contents yield the same digest across CI runners. 2) Emit per-chart SHA256 digests for the packaged .tgz artifacts, to be consumed by the bundle builder (in `redwood` repo) when generating `bundle-manifest.json`. 3) Minor metadata normalization across charts: ensure Chart.yaml `version` is semver without a leading `v`, normalize `appVersion` to match release version, and remove/avoid non-deterministic annotations.

Manifest output (example): the bundle builder will add entries like: `"helmCharts":[{"name":"redwood-control-plane","version":"1.24.0","path":"charts/redwood-control-plane-1.24.0.tgz","sha256":"<hex>"}]`.

Notes on determinism: Helm’s default packaging includes tar/gzip metadata that can vary by environment (mtime, gzip header timestamp). The new script enforces deterministic tar headers and uses `gzip -n` so that digests remain stable and are suitable for offline verification.

Testing: `make lint` (helm lint + yamllint), `make package-offline` (packages all charts and writes `dist/offline/CHARTS.json`), and `make test` (script unit tests for digest generation). CI runs packaging twice and asserts digests match.

Rollout/coordination: Depends on `redwood` PR that wires this into offline bundle assembly and manifest generation. Once merged, release pipeline can start consuming `dist/offline/*.tgz` plus `CHARTS.json`.

Checklist: - [x] Deterministic packaging (stable digest across runs) - [x] Chart metadata normalization where needed - [x] CI coverage for digest stability - [x] Docs/comments in script for how/why determinism is enforced

Related: ENG-3912 (bundle format/manifest), ENG-3916 (SBOM/provenance links in bundle).
commits: scripts: add deterministic chart packaging for offline bundles
packaging: emit per-chart sha256 digests (CHARTS.json) for bundle builder
ci: add digest stability check (package twice, compare sha256s)
docs: add README snippet for offline chart packaging output
notable_snippet: package_charts.sh now uses: `tar --sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -czf ... | gzip -n` (implemented in script form) to avoid timestamped gzip headers and non-deterministic tar mtimes. Digest is computed over the final .tgz bytes via `sha256sum`.
review_conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can you confirm the digest is over the final .tgz bytes (post gzip) and not an intermediate tar? We need the exact artifact the customer transfers to be verifiable.
Devon Price: Yep — digest is computed over the `dist/offline/*.tgz` output. I added a comment in `compute_digests.sh` and a CI check that repackages twice to verify stable tgz digests.

Ethan Park: The manifest consumer in the installer expects paths relative to the bundle root. Please ensure the exported paths are `charts/<name>-<version>.tgz` and not runner-specific `dist/...` paths.
Devon Price: Good catch. Updated `CHARTS.json` to emit bundle-relative `path` and kept `dist/offline/` as build output only. Bundle builder can copy the tgz files under `charts/`.

Marcus Lin: Metadata normalization looks fine. Please avoid including any CI runner identifiers or timestamps in Chart annotations/labels; those will create digest drift and also leak environment details.
Devon Price: Removed the last remaining `buildTimestamp` annotation and added a guard in the script to fail if prohibited annotations are present in packaged output.
Irene Choi: Any concerns with BSD tar vs GNU tar differences for the `--sort/--mtime` flags?

Devon Price: CI uses GNU tar in our build container. Script checks for GNU tar and prints a clear error suggesting to run `make package-offline` in the provided container image; added that to the README snippet.
release_notes: Offline bundles: Helm charts are now packaged deterministically and publish per-chart SHA256 digests for inclusion in the offline bundle manifest.
